meters.label: Existing clients affected by the last change

frames.narration: One Device interface offers 8 methods: print, setPaper, scan, scanToEmail, fax, faxStatus, status and reset. Five clients use it, each calling only two methods. The basic printer can do 4 of the 8.
The basic printer has to implement scan, scanToEmail, fax and faxStatus anyway. They throw NotImplemented. Nothing in the types warns a caller before it fails at runtime.
A staple method is added to Device. The office machine implements it. The basic printer must add a stub, and all 5 clients are affected, though none of them calls staple.
A LabelPrinter can only print and report status. With the fat interface it must write 7 stubs, and the code base now holds 12.

Split by what clients need: Printing, Scanning, Faxing and Admin. The basic printer implements Printing and Admin and has no stubs. Staple becomes a new Finishing role that no existing client depends on.
Roles are a compromise. The label printer prints but has no paper tray, so it still writes 2 stubs: setPaper in Printing and reset in Admin. A change to print affects only the 2 clients of Printing.

One method per interface removes every stub, but the family now has 9 interfaces, and a client that needs two methods depends on two interfaces. The cost has moved from stubs to names and dependencies.
Cut interfaces by client need, stop when a client needs nothing it does not use, and treat a stub that throws as the signal to split. Do not split to one method everywhere.
